# Glaurung CLI reference

> **Kind:** reference · **Status:** generated
<!-- generated by tools/gen_cli_reference.py at a014dd51; do not edit -->

Every subcommand `uv run glaurung --help` prints, generated from the live `argparse` parsers in `python/glaurung/cli/commands/`. 41 commands, in the order `python/glaurung/cli/main.py`'s `_REGISTRY` declares them. Regenerate with `uv run python tools/gen_cli_reference.py` after any parser change; `--check` fails the build when this file is stale.

## Common flags

Every command accepts these, added once by `BaseCommand.add_common_arguments`:

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format {plain,rich,json,jsonl}` | `'plain'` | Output format (default: plain) |
| `--json` | `False` | Alias for --format json |
| `--no-color` | `False` | Disable colored output (forces plain format) |
| `--quiet, -q` | `False` | Suppress non-essential output |
| `--verbose, -v` | `False` | Enable verbose output |

## `glaurung disasm`

```
glaurung disasm [options] <path>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Path to file |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--engine {auto,iced,capstone}` | `'auto'` | Disassembler engine to use |
| `--arch {x86,x86_64,arm,arm64,mips,mips64,ppc,ppc64,riscv,riscv64,unknown}` | `None` | Target architecture |
| `--window-bytes WINDOW_BYTES` | `8192` | Number of bytes to read (pre-2026-05-25 default was 256) |
| `--max-instructions MAX_INSTRUCTIONS` | `2048` | Maximum instructions to disassemble (pre-2026-05-25 default was 32, way too low for real functions) |
| `--max-time-ms MAX_TIME_MS` | `5000` | Maximum time in milliseconds (pre-2026-05-25 default was 20, way too tight for any real binary) |
| `--addr ADDR` | `None` | Starting virtual address (e.g., 0x1000) |
| `--entry` | `True` | Start at detected entrypoint if available (default) |
| `--no-entry` | `True` | Do not use entrypoint; start at VA 0 or --addr |
| `--comments` | `False` | Add comments for calls and strings |
| `--db DB` | `None` | A .glaurung project. With --function, disassemble one function with symbol-annotated call targets, CFG-derived bounds, and a coverage footer (KB-aware mode). |
| `--function NAME|VA` | `None` | Function to disassemble in KB-aware mode: a canonical/demangled name or a hex/decimal VA. Requires --db. |

## `glaurung ask`

```
glaurung ask [options] <path>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Path to binary file to analyze |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-a, --ask QUESTION` | `None` | Question to ask about the binary |
| `-m, --multiple QUESTIONS` | `None` | Multiple questions to ask |
| `-i, --interactive` | `False` | Interactive Q&A mode |
| `--stdin` | `False` | Read questions from stdin (one per line) |
| `--agent {memory,simple}` | `'memory'` | Agent backend to use (default: memory) |
| `--strategy {single,iterative,auto}` | `'auto'` | Execution strategy: single-pass, iterative refinement, or auto-select (default: auto) |
| `--max-iterations MAX_ITERATIONS` | `5` | Max iterations for iterative strategy (default: 5) |
| `--min-confidence MIN_CONFIDENCE` | `0.7` | Minimum confidence threshold for iterative strategy (default: 0.7) |
| `--timeout TIMEOUT` | `120` | Maximum execution time in seconds (default: 120) |
| `--show-tools` | `False` | Show tool calls and results (verbose mode) |
| `--show-plan` | `False` | Show LLM planning/reasoning |
| `--model MODEL` | `None` | Model to use (default: openai:gpt-5.4-mini) |
| `--max-read-bytes MAX_READ_BYTES` | `10485760` | Max bytes to read during triage (default: 10MB) |
| `--max-file-size MAX_FILE_SIZE` | `104857600` | Max file size (default: 100MB) |
| `--quick` | `False` | Quick mode: ask common malware analysis questions |
| `--max-functions MAX_FUNCTIONS` | `5` | Max functions to analyze |
| `--max-instructions MAX_INSTRUCTIONS` | `50000` | Max instructions budget |
| `--disasm-window DISASM_WINDOW` | `4096` | Max disassembly window bytes |
| `--findings-json PATH` | `None` | Run a structured-output pass that returns a FindingsReport (list of VulnerabilityFinding) and write it to PATH as JSON. PATH '-' writes to stdout. Independent of -a/--ask: the structured pass uses a fixed vuln-discovery prompt. After discovery, the L4 cite-or-discard verifier resolves cited references and the L2 self-critique pass grades each finding's evidence. |
| `--skip-critique` | `False` | Skip the L2 self-critique pass (one extra LLM call per finding). Use when iterating cheaply; the L4 verifier still runs. |
| `--cwe-sweep` | `False` | Run the L3 CWE-class sweep (one structured pass per CWE family in the catalog) instead of a single broad discovery pass. Implies --findings-json; pass --findings-json PATH to choose the output location (default: stdout). Each per-class pass still goes through L4 verification and L2 critique. |
| `--cwe-sweep-applies {any,userland,kernel}` | `'any'` | Filter the CWE sweep catalog to classes applicable to userland or kernel code. Default 'any' runs every class. |
| `--route` | `False` | L5: route the question to a focused tool subset (5-30 tools) instead of loading all 163. The router is deterministic keyword matching; intents include vuln_discovery, triage_summary, function_walk, import_audit, string_audit, and a broad_discovery fallback. Combine with --show-routing to see which intent matched. |
| `--show-routing` | `False` | Print the selected intent + tool subset before running. |
| `--all-tools` | `False` | Force the legacy behaviour: register every tool the memory agent knows. Overrides --route. |
| `--max-cost-usd USD` | `None` | F5 cost circuit breaker. Set a hard upper bound (in USD) on the LLM spend for THIS invocation. When the running session cost exceeds USD, the next agent call raises CostBudgetExceeded; partial findings (per CWE class) are still written. Use this as defense-in-depth on top of --cwe-sweep / sweep wrappers. |
| `--usage-log PATH` | `None` | Path to write JSONL usage records (one line per LLM call). Default: ~/.cache/glaurung/usage/<session>.jsonl. Set to '-' to disable file logging (in-memory only). |

## `glaurung decompile`

```
glaurung decompile [options] <path>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Path to file |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--analysis-config ANALYSIS_CONFIG` | `None` | Optional Windows analysis config YAML/JSON. Defaults to .glaurung/windows-analysis.yaml or $GLAURUNG_WINDOWS_ANALYSIS_CONFIG when present. |
| `--func FUNC` | `None` | Function selector: hex VA (0x140001480), decimal, or a function name like 'main' resolved against analysis. If omitted, the detected entry point is used. Stripped binaries only have sub_<VA> names so VA is preferred. |
| `--all` | `False` | Decompile up to --limit discovered functions instead of one. |
| `--vas VAS|@FILE|-` | `None` | Decompile exactly these entry VAs (each hex 0x... or decimal) in a single analysis pass. Accepts an inline comma/space-separated list, @FILE to read them from a file, or - to read them from stdin; a file or stdin may also use one VA per line and may carry # comments. Emits a JSON list of {name, entry_va, pseudocode}. Intended for batch/benchmark harnesses that already know their target function set (e.g. DWARF low_pc addresses) -- @FILE and - carry no argv length bound, so a caller never has to split or cap a target set. Entries that recover no body are named on stderr and omitted from the list; exits 2 only when no requested entry recovers at all. |
| `--limit LIMIT` | `8` | Max number of functions to decompile with --all (default: 8). |
| `--no-types` | `True` | Disable type-annotation pass in the output. |
| `--timeout-ms TIMEOUT_MS` | `None` | Per-function analysis timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to analysis config. |
| `--max-blocks MAX_BLOCKS` | `None` | Per-function max basic blocks. Defaults to analysis config. |
| `--max-instructions MAX_INSTRUCTIONS` | `None` | Per-function max instructions. Defaults to analysis config. |
| `--range-start RANGE_START` | `None` | Explicit function range start VA for range-seeded decompile. |
| `--range-end RANGE_END` | `None` | Explicit exclusive function range end VA for range-seeded decompile. |
| `--style {plain,c,decbench}` | `'plain'` | Pseudocode style: 'plain' keeps the register-level detail (default); 'c' strips the %% prefix and annotations for a closer-to-C view; 'decbench' emits parseable C (a real 'long name(long arg0, ...)' signature with declared locals) for external tooling that parses the output as C. |
| `--pdb-cache PDB_CACHE` | `''` | Optional Microsoft-style PDB cache directory used to resolve PE/PDB public function names in decompile output. |
| `--cache-dir CACHE_DIR` | `None` | Optional persistent cache directory for single-function decompile output. Entries are keyed by (glaurung version, sha256(binary), VA, decompile flags). Falls back to $GLAURUNG_CACHE_DIR when unset. Append-only — clear the directory manually if disk fills up. |
| `--db DB` | `None` | Optional .glaurung project file. Function names recorded in the project (an analyst rename, a DWARF or FLIRT name) are applied to the decompiled output -- at the definition AND at every call site. Without it this command is blind to the project, so a renamed function still prints as sub_<hex>. |

## `glaurung explain`

```
glaurung explain [options] <path>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Path to file |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--func FUNC` | `None` | Entry VA of the function to explain (hex or decimal). If omitted, the detected entry point is used. |
| `--range-start RANGE_START` | `None` | Start VA of a byte window to disassemble (hex/decimal). Use with --range-end to seed the decompiler at an arbitrary VA without whole-binary function discovery -- required on large stripped binaries where auto-discovery is slow or misses the target (e.g. 'no function at entry VA'). Defaults to --func when --range-end is given. |
| `--range-end RANGE_END` | `None` | End VA (exclusive) of the byte window. Required when --range-start is set. A window of ~0x4000 past the entry is typical for one function. |
| `--style {c,rust,go}` | `'c'` | Target language for the rewritten source (default: c). |
| `--no-types` | `True` | Skip Tool #10 (signature inference); use a minimal placeholder prototype like 'int sub_<va>(void *)'. |
| `--no-roles` | `True` | Skip Tool #13 (role classification) -- the rewriter still runs, just without a role hint. |
| `--with-layer0` | `False` | Enable the F4 Layer-0 atomic-labeler pre-pass: runs Tools #5 / #3 / #2 to populate variable_names / string_names / constant_labels before Tool #14. Adds 10-30 LLM calls per function (~$0.20-$0.50). Off by default. A7 cache via --cache-dir / GLAURUNG_CACHE_DIR amortizes cost across CVE months. |
| `--no-layer0` | `True` | Force-disable the F4 Layer-0 pre-pass (default). |
| `--timeout-ms TIMEOUT_MS` | `2000` | Per-stage analysis / LLM timeout in milliseconds (default: 2000). |
| `--pdb-cache PDB_CACHE` | `''` | Optional Microsoft-style PDB cache directory used by the underlying decompile pass for call-target name resolution. |
| `--cache-dir CACHE_DIR` | `None` | Optional A7 persistent cache directory. With --with-layer0 each Layer-0 call (Tool #5 / #3 / #2) is cached by (binary sha, va, kind, input). Falls back to $GLAURUNG_CACHE_DIR when unset. Tool #10 / Tool #14 themselves remain uncached for now. |
| `--fidelity {tldr,annotated}` | `'tldr'` | Rewrite preset. 'tldr' (default) = idiomatic compressed rewrite for source recovery / readability. 'annotated' = per-basic-block faithful for bug-hunting triage; emits a block list with start_va/end_va/lifted_c plus enumerated calls/mem_accesses/branches per block. Use 'annotated' when feeding the output to a vulnerability reviewer. |
| `--suspicious-va SUSPICIOUS_VAS` | `[]` | VA (hex/decimal) of a region a static rule fired on. Repeatable. The annotated rewriter biases attention here -- blocks containing these VAs are emitted with extra fidelity. |
| `--require-llm` | `False` | Hard-fail (non-zero exit) when the LLM is unreachable instead of silently degrading to the heuristic fallback. Recommended for automation/batch pipelines where heuristic output downstream would be mistaken for an LLM lift. Same effect as GLAURUNG_REQUIRE_LLM=1. |

## `glaurung diff`

```
glaurung diff [options] <binary_a> <binary_b>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `binary_a` | First binary ("before") |
| `binary_b` | Second binary ("after") |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--include-anonymous` | `False` | Include `sub_<hex>` placeholder functions in the diff. Off by default — their VAs shift between builds and the resulting noise dominates real changes. |
| `--max-rows MAX_ROWS` | `0` | Cap on changed-function rows shown in Markdown output. 0 = unlimited. JSON output is never truncated regardless. |
| `--pdb-cache PDB_CACHE` | `''` | Optional Microsoft-style PDB cache directory. When set, each row's JSON output carries `public_name_pre` / `public_name_post` populated from the PDB at the row's entry VA -- skips LLM-naming for nameable functions. |
| `--cross-name-threshold CROSS_NAME_THRESHOLD` | `None` | Jaccard-similarity cutoff for the v3 cross-name rematch pass (Diaphora-style). Pairs of unmatched added/removed rows scoring at or above this value get collapsed into a single `changed` row. Set to 1.01 to disable the pass. Default: 0.85. |
| `--no-structural-rematch` | `False` | Skip the L1 structural pass. On by default: it ranks the changed table by how far the MD-index, block/edge counts, mnemonic product and rare constants moved, and re-pairs added/removed rows whose control-flow shape is globally rare (Diaphora's `count <= 2` rule) and identical on both sides. Costs one extra discovery pass per binary. |

## `glaurung kickoff`

```
glaurung kickoff [options] <path>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--db DB` | `None` | .glaurung project file to persist results into. Defaults to a fresh tmp file. |
| `--session SESSION` | `'main'` | KB session name (default: main) |
| `--max-functions MAX_FUNCTIONS` | `64` | Cap on functions analysed for stack-frame / propagation / struct lifts. |
| `--max-file-size MAX_FILE_SIZE` | `104857600` | Max file size to triage/analyze in bytes (default 100MB). Raise for large binaries. |
| `--max-read-bytes MAX_READ_BYTES` | `10000000` | Max bytes read during triage (default 10MB). |
| `--analyze-packed` | `False` | Analyse a binary even when packer detection flags it. Default: skip deep analysis on packed binaries. |
| `--pdb-cache PDB_CACHE` | `None` | Microsoft-style PDB cache dir for symbol naming. Defaults to $GLAURUNG_PDB_CACHE / a local _NT_SYMBOL_PATH dir / ~/.cache/glaurung/symbols. |
| `--no-pdb` | `True` | Disable PDB public-symbol naming (default: on for PE with a CodeView record). |
| `--no-fetch-pdb` | `True` | Do not download a missing PDB from the Microsoft symbol server; use only what is already cached. |
| `--pdb-struct NAME` | `None` | Import this PDB struct's layout into the type DB during kickoff (repeatable). Unlisted structs stay on-demand. |

## `glaurung patch`

```
glaurung patch [options] <input> <output>
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | Source binary |
| `output` | Output binary path |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--va VA` | `None` | Virtual address to patch (hex with 0x or decimal) |
| `--bytes PAYLOAD` | `None` | Hex byte payload, e.g. "90 90 90" or "488b45f8" |
| `--nop` | `False` | NOP out the instruction at --va (size-preserving) |
| `--jmp JMP_TARGET` | `None` | Replace the instruction at --va with `jmp <target>` (size-preserving, NOP-padded). Argument is target VA. |
| `--force-branch {true,false}` | `None` | Force the conditional branch at --va: true = always taken (JMP to original target); false = always not taken (NOPs). |
| `--verify` | `False` | After patching, re-disassemble at --va and print the resulting instruction so the analyst can confirm the byte-level change decodes as intended. |
| `--force` | `False` | Overwrite output if it exists |

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output-format {json,markdown,header,ida,binja,ghidra,bundle}` | `'markdown'` | Export shape (default: markdown). `json` is round-trippable; `header` emits the type DB as .h; `ida` / `binja` / `ghidra` emit scripts that apply the KB inside the respective tool; `bundle` is the whole-binary artifact — functions with their boundaries, prototypes, stack variables, xrefs and content-derived identity, and with --bodies their decompiled C. |

## `glaurung windows`

```
glaurung windows [options] {diff-ghidra,ioctl,analyst,analyst-loop,analyst-notebook,corpus-guard,high-volume-preflight,project-fact-manifest,project-xrefs,project-callgraph-reachability,project-callgraph-diff,project-guard-condition-diff,project-function-chunks,project-function-boundary-diff,project-function-start-explain,project-symbol-ranges,project-memory-access-query,project-memory-access-diff,project-data-tables,project-data-table-diff,project-prototype-diff,bootstrap-project-facts,blocker-task-plan,symbol-similarity-plan,function-similarity-manifest,runner-artifact-review,runner-artifact-promotion-plan,runner-artifact-promotion-apply,target-pipeline} ...
```

Subcommands (`windows_action`):

| Subcommand | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `diff-ghidra` | Compare Glaurung function starts with a Ghidra parity JSON report |
| `ioctl` | Map a Windows driver's IOCTL attack surface (dispatchers, codes, MSVC switch jump tables, handlers) |
| `analyst` | Ask the deterministic Windows analyst workflow a bounded question |
| `analyst-loop` | Run a bounded multi-turn Windows analyst command script |
| `analyst-notebook` | Import or export analyst notebook decisions for a .glaurung Windows project |
| `corpus-guard` | Check vendored Windows corpus manifest/dashboard/local-file drift |
| `high-volume-preflight` | Check runner readiness for high-volume Windows target-pipeline runs |
| `project-fact-manifest` | Inspect ASB .glaurung project fact coverage records |
| `project-xrefs` | Run IDA/Ghidra-style callers, callees, reads, writes, refs-to, or refs-from queries over a .glaurung project |
| `project-callgraph-reachability` | Find bounded source-to-target or upstream-to-target callgraph paths in a .glaurung project |
| `project-callgraph-diff` | Compare persisted call/jump xrefs across two .glaurung projects for patch/build diff triage |
| `project-guard-condition-diff` | Compare persisted branch guards and callsite path conditions across two .glaurung projects for patch/build diff triage |
| `project-function-chunks` | Query function chunk, thunk, tailcall, and shared-tail facts from a .glaurung project |
| `project-function-boundary-diff` | Compare function boundaries, chunks, thunks, tailcalls, and funclets across two .glaurung projects |
| `project-function-start-explain` | Explain why a VA or symbol is a function, thunk, chunk, or candidate in a .glaurung project |
| `project-symbol-ranges` | Audit PDB/public symbol ranges against .pdata, symbol adjacency, containing ranges, and chunk facts |
| `project-memory-access-query` | Query persisted memory_operand_facts for reads, writes, fields, base objects, and data targets |
| `project-memory-access-diff` | Compare persisted memory_operand_facts across two .glaurung projects for field/global/buffer read/write drift |
| `project-data-tables` | Recover project dispatch tables, callback arrays, vtables, jump tables, import thunk tables, and code-pointer tables |
| `project-data-table-diff` | Compare recovered dispatch tables, callback arrays, vtables, jump tables, import thunk tables, and code-pointer tables across two .glaurung projects |
| `project-prototype-diff` | Compare function prototypes across two .glaurung projects for patch/build diff triage |
| `bootstrap-project-facts` | Create or update a .glaurung Windows PE project fact cache |
| `blocker-task-plan` | Turn high-volume preflight and target-pipeline blocker artifacts into concrete follow-up tasks |
| `symbol-similarity-plan` | Plan PDB/symbol-server and BSim extraction for a Windows patch pair |
| `function-similarity-manifest` | Generate a deterministic Glaurung opcode/body similarity manifest for a patch pair |
| `runner-artifact-review` | Review high-volume Windows runner artifacts for blockers and baseline-promotion readiness |
| `runner-artifact-promotion-plan` | Plan reviewed runner artifact promotion into docs/metadata baselines |
| `runner-artifact-promotion-apply` | Verify and optionally apply reviewed runner artifact promotion plans |
| `target-pipeline` | Run deterministic target triage, packet emission, review, and evidence checks |

## `glaurung locks`

```
glaurung locks [options] [path]
```

Positional arguments:

| Argument | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Binary path (optional; resolved from --db if omitted) |

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--db DB` | `None` | .glaurung project to read symbols from |
| `--function NAME|VA` | `None` | Function name (canonical/demangled) or VA |

## `glaurung group`

```
glaurung group [options]
```

Options (beyond the [common flags](#common-flags)):

| Flag | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--member NAME=BINARY` | `None` | A group member as name=path/to/driver.sys (repeatable, >=2) |

## `glaurung sigs`

```
glaurung sigs [options] {list,fetch,verify,status,path} ...
```

Subcommands (`sigs_action`):

| Subcommand | Help |
| --- | --- |
| `list` | List the blobs in the active manifest |
| `fetch` | Download and verify a signature set |
| `verify` | Re-verify the cached manifest signature and every blob |
| `status` | What the cache holds and how it was verified |
| `path` | Print resolved paths |
